source.wiki_title: Don't Clam Up on Me Now

identity.dat_name: Don't Clam Up on Me Now

notes: Three bullets, three steps, and the middle one is the only judgement call. 'Shellfish' resolves as an entity key but NOT as an item and NOT as a key item, so the five you collect are a hidden server-side count -- nothing in the packets sees them. Evidence is therefore null on step 2 rather than an invented 'Shellfish x5', and the mark simply stays on the beach until you go back to Oblor. That is the honest answer and it is also the reason the page's warning matters: zoning loses all five and no ladder could tell. The two beaches at (K-7) and (K-8) are alternatives, not both required, so the step carries no grid and names both in the note -- picking one would be arbitrary. Both NMs are recorded as spawns because they are what a player will actually see; the page is explicit that they need not be killed and drop nothing. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions the addon knows, so it gates nothing and only the raw string survives.

steps.note: at the Frontier Station

five of them, on either beach on the east side: (K-7) among the Orobons or (K-8) among the Uragnites -- so no single grid is recorded. Locations are semi-random, a replacement spawns immediately, and the same clam cannot be taken twice by anyone. The count is not observable and neither is the shellfish itself. Do NOT zone while carrying them; all five are lost.

notes:
A clean three-rung ladder. Bullets 2 and 3 are one action, not two: 'head to the Fay Pond at (F-5)' is where the trade in bullet 3 happens, and splitting them would put an unmarkable travel rung in front of a perfectly markable object. Fay Pond resolves as a real entity key, so this quest gets a marker in the middle of Abyssea - Grauberg rather than only at its giver. The header gives no grid for Rukususu (A); the walkthrough gives (F-10), so that is carried into start rather than left blank. The Pinch of pixie dust is a random drop from the trade -- the page says bring multiple Twinkle Powder -- so the ladder can stall on step 2 for many trades, which is correct: you really are not done. That key item is step 2's evidence and step 3's requirement, which is the ordinary hand-in shape and not a duplicate. The unnumbered lines top and bottom are both preconditions about zoning, not steps.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: The key item is a random result, so bring several powders; the count needed cannot be expressed.

notes: A five-rung errand between Upper Jeuno, La Theine Plateau and Southern San d'Oria, and every rung is markable: Chocobo Tracks resolves as an entity key, so step 2 is a real marker and not a bare grid reference. Bullets 5 and 6 are merged: both are Brutus at (G-7), which is one marker whichever way it is written, and nothing observable separates them -- the only difference is that you must let a game day pass AND zone back into Upper Jeuno before the egg cutscene fires, which no packet reports. Nothing in this quest is observable at all: the Chocobo Egg is the header's Reward, so by the reward rule it proves the quest is over rather than a step done, and every evidence field is null. The trailing 'Optional:' line is not a step -- trading the egg to a VCS Trainer starts Chocobo Raising, a different system entirely, and the page names no one trainer. Bullet 4's warning that all three answers are wrong but must be chosen anyway is dialogue, not a rung.

steps.note: choose to help the chocobo leave when prompted
far northwest corner of (E-5), just south of the sliver of map in (E-4)
three choices are offered and all three are wrong; the page says pick 'Bring the chocobos together'

two visits merged, same NPC and same marker: the first completes the quest, then one game day later he hands over the Chocobo Egg. You must zone out and back into Upper Jeuno after the day change -- logging out and in does not count.

notes: Bullet 1 is not a step -- 'make sure you do not leave without picking up a few Pickaxe' is packing advice, and the pickaxes belong where they are actually used, as the mining step's requirement. The mining itself has no named target: the page says only 'begin mine in this room', so the target is none rather than an invented rock, and the step keeps its place on the strength of its zone and grid. Its evidence is the one genuine OR in this quest -- Electrocell, Electropot or Electrolocomotive, any single one -- written as an empty AND-list with three alternates, the same idiom the index already uses for the Mandragora quest. That same three-way choice is restated as the hand-in requirement on step 5, split one-plus-two so the requirement list is never vacuously empty. Both rewards are header Rewards and neither is evidence: the Lightning Band arrives at the hand-in, and the Olduum Ring only exists after the optional bullet 6, which happens AFTER the quest is already complete and is therefore marked optional rather than dropped -- the repeat section depends on holding that ring. The sub-bullet warning about 'approaching the platform will complete this quest' sits under the Blue Mage flag quest remark and most likely means that quest, not this one; recorded as written.

any one of the three artifacts; written as one plus two alternates so the requirement is never an empty list. He rewards the Lightning Band, which is a header Reward and so not evidence.
the quest is already complete at step 4; this turns the Lightning Band into the Olduum Ring. Optional, but dropping the ring is what lets Dkhaaya repeat the quest.

notes: A three-rung fetch entirely inside Abyssea - Attohwa. Bullet 2 is not a talk -- 'she will ask you for x3' is the outcome of bullet 1's conversation, and its sub-bullet is where the pseudopods come from, so bullet 2 becomes the farming step rather than a second visit to Ponono. The item is written twice on the page, once short ('Amb. Pseudopod') and once long ('Amoeban Pseudopod'); both resolve to the same id and the long form is used. The farming step keeps a zone because the page names a real place for it -- around Veridical Conflux #00 -- even though the Auction House is an alternative that has no zone at all; holding three is genuine evidence either way. Red Ghost (A) is not a step: he is the lift you need only if Conflux #08 is not yet unlocked, which is a precondition and is noted on step 1 instead. The 25-completions fame remark and the no-zoning-to-repeat line are neither of them steps.

notes: Bullets 3 and 4 are one instruction split across two lines: three map locations, and the thing you do at each of them. They become three group members sharing 'rafflesia', one per grid, all in Yuhtunga Jungle -- the page gives no order, so a strict ladder would mark (F-7) and nothing else until you happened to walk there. Blue Rafflesia is a real entity name and all three carry markers. VERIFY REMOVED the evidence on the last group member: Rafflesia Nectar x3 is the header's Reward field word for word, and hard rule 7 says a reward proves the quest is over rather than a step done. The draft argued an exception -- that these are handed over one per flower DURING the quest -- but the rules grant no such exception, and an unordered group has no last member for the mark to sit on anyway; (I-12) was chosen only because it is written last on the page. The quest is now unobservable end to end, which is honest but weaker, so it is demoted to medium. The step 5 claim that 'you keep the three nectars' was also cut: the page nowhere says so. Bullet 1 and the Notes bullet 6 are the same zoning precondition stated twice and are not steps; bullet 7 (Mithra repulsed, Opo-opos attracted) is a consequence. The gil is a real requirement but 15,000-35,000 gil is neither an item nor a fixed amount, so it lives in the note.

notes: The whole middle of this quest is seven avatar battlefields, and the page names no zone for any of them -- only the seven quests they belong to and the seven items you pick as their reward. So it is ONE step, unzoned and unmarkable, exactly like the six battles in Waking the Beast: seven rungs a player cannot be tracked through would be noise, and inventing the Cloisters from the avatar names is the guessing this rebuild exists to avoid. The avatars themselves ARE named in the page, so they are recorded as mobs with role kill; the item is a reward selection after the win rather than a drop. The evidence is an alternates-only list of all seven, not an AND-list, and that is the load-bearing decision: bullet 3 says the items are traded ONE AT A TIME and need not all be turned in at once, so a player may never hold all seven simultaneously and an AND-list would never fire. Holding any one means 'go trade it', which is precisely what the ladder should say. The hand-in requirement is written the same way. Bullet 4 is a separate rung on the same NPC, kept because midnight JST genuinely divides it from the trading, and flagged time_gated since nothing in the packets sees game time. The Evoker's Ring is the header Reward and is never evidence. The After-the-walkthrough Notes section holds one bullet, numbered [1] in its own sequence, and it is a repeat condition rather than a step. Confidence is medium because the seven-item middle is a single opaque step and the whole ladder hangs on it.

steps.note: the page is explicit that this need not be done before collecting the seven items

seven battlefields, one per avatar, entered through Trial by Fire / Ice / Wind / Earth / Lightning / Water and The Moonlit Path; each item is chosen as the battle's reward. The page names no zone for any of them, so none is recorded. Alternates, not an AND-list: any one item in hand means there is something to trade.
all seven eventually, but one at a time and not necessarily in one visit -- so the requirement is written as alternates and holding any single item is enough to be ready
only after midnight JST has passed; he then hands over the Evoker's Ring, which is the header Reward and so not evidence. Same NPC as step 3, so one marker.

notes: Six bullets and only three of them are things you do. Bullet 2 is not a step -- 'when the cutscene ends you will have obtained a [KI] Bouquet for the pioneers' is the outcome of bullet 1, so it becomes step 1's evidence, which is where the key item is actually granted. Bullet 4 and all the sub-bullets under 3 and 4 are route advice for climbing Zegham Hill: which ramps, which survival guide, which direction round the plateau. None of that is a rung; it is one walk to one object. VERIFY NULLED that object's name. The draft called it 'Monument'; the page only ever writes 'find a monument at J-7', 'Touch the monument', and the description's 'the monument honoring the Palborough Pioneers' -- a common noun with an article, which is exactly the 'the baskets' case hard rule 1 sends to {none, null}. The draft's defence, that 'Monument' folds to a clean entity key, proves nothing: the npc resolver is a normaliser, not an existence check, and it folds 'the baskets' and outright nonsense just as happily. The step keeps its place on North Gustaberg (J-7) but cannot carry a marker, so the quest goes to medium. A human with the game open could restore a name here; this pass cannot invent one.

steps.note: in the Bat's Lair Inn; the cutscene both starts the quest and grants the bouquet

at the peak of Zegham Hill. Fastest in is the Oldton Movalpolos survival guide, out to North Gustaberg, then up from the middle of (I-6); alternatively the Port Bastok exit by Home Point #1 and up the southwest side at the (H-8)/(I-8) border. On the first plateau go counter-clockwise to the ramp in the middle of (J-8), then round the hill again to the last ramp. The page never names this object -- only 'a monument', 'the monument' -- so the target is unnamed and the rung rests on zone and grid.

notes: The canonical two-rung Gobbiebag shape, and the reason items_alt exists: the Goblin Stew 880 REPLACES all four crafted items rather than joining them, so the four are the AND-list and the stew is the single alternate. Both branches resolve. The page writes 'a Square of Peiste Leather' and 'a square of Oil-Soaked Cloth'; 'square of' is the crafting unit, not part of either item name, and both resolve without it. Nothing here is evidence -- the reward is an inventory increase, which is an outcome and not something you can hold, so both steps have null evidence and the ladder rests on the trade requirement instead. The '== Required Item Comparison ==' table is a gil cost comparison as of August 2019 and holds no instruction; the flag is set only so a human knows a table was read and rejected. The sub-bullets under bullet 2 are Auction House categories.

steps.note: in Muckvix's Junk Shop
the four items together, OR the stew on its own. All are on the Auction House, though Peiste Skins only farm in Wings of the Goddess areas.

notes:
The page contradicts itself about where this quest ends: bullet 2 says the second Joachim cutscene completes it, and then bullet 3 sends you to the Hall of the Gods anyway, which is what the header's own description asks for ('make your way to the Hall of the Gods, deep within Ro'Maeve'). All three are kept in page order and the quest is demoted to medium for it; dropping bullet 3 would silently lose the only step outside Port Jeuno, and Hall of the Gods turns out to be a zone in its own right, so that step keeps a place. The real gate -- six of nine listed quests for the first cutscene, seven for the second -- is a count nothing reports, but each threshold hands over an abyssite, and holding an abyssite IS observable, so the two abyssites become the two steps' requirements. That is the whole modelling win here. 'Lunar abyssite' does not resolve: the name is shared by more than one key item id and the resolver rejects rather than guesses, so that entry will be dropped and step 2 falls back to being a plain marker on Joachim. Neither abyssite is used as evidence, because both are earned in OTHER quests and not at these steps. The header's Previous field mixes one quest with three expansion storylines under an 'Expansion Set Quests:' label; all four titles are recorded as written. Fame 'Abyssea' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.
